title: Enter Website
rationale: Starts with a fresh browser context; the application server is seeded with initial notes. Opening the root URL should render the home page, which includes the 'Take a note' editor entry and the seeded notes list.

title: Note Listing
rationale: Opening the entry URL renders the seeded home page. The pinned seed note 'Sprint goals' and the regular seed note 'Groceries' are the observable note cards from the state contract, so asserting both visible texts checks the notes list and the pinned/regular seed set.

then.detail: The exact section heading or visual separator text for pinned vs regular notes is not declared in the contract exact-text list, so the two seeded cards are asserted individually.

title: Create Note
rationale: The 'Take a note' composer is the declared navigation control for entering the note editor. Unique scenario-derived title and content are filled in the expanded editor, the editor is closed with Escape to commit autosave, and the new note card is asserted by its generated title and content.

given.source: Scenario-derived unique title for the note created in REQ-2.2; it does not collide with any seeded note title.
Scenario-derived unique content for the same created note, allowing an unambiguous visible-text assertion.

title: Delete
rationale: The system seeds the unpinned note titled 'Delete me 2.3.1'. From the home page, hover over that note to reveal its More options button, open the menu, and choose Delete Note. Verify the note disappears from the main list and the delete notification with Undo is displayed.

title: Notification and Undo
rationale: The scenario requires a note that has just been deleted, so the seeded note 'Delete me 2.3.2' is deleted first through the More options menu. After the delete notification appears, clicking Undo should restore the note and display the 'Action undone' notification. The note is keyed by its unique seed title.

title: Trash list
rationale: The seeded note 'Delete me 2.3.3' is initially active, so it is deleted first to put an item in the trash. Then the sidebar Trash link is used to navigate to the Trash list, where the deleted note should be visible.

title: Update Note
rationale: The seeded note 'Project ideas' has initial content 'Initial editable content'. Opening its card, replacing the content with a unique scenario-derived string, and closing the editor verifies persistence when the updated content is rendered and the old initial content is absent.

given.source: Scenario-derived unique replacement content for the seeded 'Project ideas' note; it does not match any existing note text.

title: Archive
rationale: The note 'Travel plans 2.5.1' is seeded as active. Archive it from its note card, then confirm it is removed from the home list, the Undo notification appears, and it is visible in the Archived view when the sidebar link is used.

title: Archive Undo
rationale: The scenario begins with the archive notification visible, so the active seed note 'Travel plans 2.5.2' is archived first. Clicking Undo should restore it to the home notes list, which is verified by its presence on the home page.

title: Show archived notes
rationale: The seed note 'Travel plans 2.5.3' is active. It must be archived first to create archived content, then the Archived sidebar item opens the archived list where the note should be visible.

title: Unarchive
rationale: The seed note 'Travel plans 2.5.4' is active. After archiving it and opening the Archived list, the Unarchive action should move it out of the archived list and back to the main Notes list, verified by its absence in Archived and presence after clicking Notes.

title: Change note color
rationale: Changes the background color of an existing seeded note ('Garden tasks existing') from the home page color palette. The note is pre-seeded, so no creation is needed. UI route: home -> hover note -> open color palette -> select light green. The final color assertion is unobservable with the available primitives (no style/color inspection), so an unknown step is emitted.

then.detail: The change to a light green background cannot be asserted with the available primitives (no style/color inspection), so this part of the THEN clause is unobservable.

title: Choose note color when created
rationale: Creates a new note through the 'Take a note' form, selects the light green color from the palette before closing the editor, then verifies the note appears in the notes list. Title/content are bound to unique values to identify the created note. The selected color itself cannot be asserted with the available primitives, so an unknown step is emitted.

when.source: Unique title to identify the note created in this scenario.

then.detail: The selected light green color of the created note cannot be asserted with available primitives (no style/color inspection).

title: Assign label to a note
rationale: The seeded note 'Team retro add label' is present on the home page and initially has no labels. Opening its More options and selecting 'Change labels' exposes the label picker; choosing 'Work' adds the label. The label chip is then visible on the note, and the Work sidebar filter shows the note. All targets are derived from the navigation entries and seeded exact texts in the contract.

title: Remove label from a note
rationale: The seeded note 'Team retro remove label' already carries the Work label, so the test starts from that state. Opening the label picker and unchecking Work removes the label; the note's card no longer shows the Work chip, and the Work sidebar filter no longer lists the note while still showing the seeded Work-labeled note 'Design review' as a positive control.

title: Default label
rationale: The sidebar exposes the labels list on the home page. 'Reminders' is seeded as a default label and should appear in that list as soon as the application opens, so no additional preparation is needed and the assertion is made after opening the entry URL. The dedicated icon cannot be asserted with the available primitives, so only the visible label text is checked.

title: Assign default label when creating note
rationale: The home page's 'Take a note' editor is opened from the entry page. A unique title and content are generated to avoid collisions with seeded notes. The editor's More options menu provides 'Change labels', where the default 'Reminders' label is selected before closing the editor; autosave persists the note. Opening the 'Reminders' sidebar filter then proves that the created note carries the default label.

given.source: Unique generated title to avoid collisions; Keep accepts arbitrary text titles.
Unique generated content for the scenario note.

title: Edit labels
rationale: The seeded label 'Work editable' is visible in the sidebar. Opening 'Edit Labels' shows the label management list; the edit control for that label is located by its accessible name containing the label text. The label is renamed to a unique value and committed with Enter. The new name appearing and the old name disappearing in the label list confirms the saved change.

given.source: Unique renamed label to avoid collisions and verify persistence.

title: View list filtered by label
rationale: Filters the notes list by selecting the Work label in the sidebar; verifies only notes with that label remain visible. Relies on seeded notes 'Design review' (Work label) and 'Movie list' (no Work or Reminders label). Inferred UI route: open home page, sidebar visible, click Work label in sidebar.

title: View all notes
rationale: Returns from a label-filtered view to the full notes list by clicking Notes in the sidebar. Preparation includes opening home and filtering by Work label to enter filtered view, then asserting the filter worked before navigating back. Inferred UI route: sidebar links for labels and Notes.

title: View Reminders
rationale: Filters notes by the default Reminders label via the sidebar; only notes with that label should appear. Relies on seeded notes 'Call dentist existing' (Reminders label) and 'Movie list' (no Reminders label). Inferred UI route: sidebar Reminders link.

title: Pin note
rationale: The seed contains an unpinned note 'Meeting agenda 2.8.1'. Open the home page, hover the note to reveal its actions, and click the pin button. Afterwards the pinned heading and the note title should be present on the home page.

title: Unpin note
rationale: The seed 'Meeting agenda 2.8.2' starts unpinned. To satisfy the pinned-state prerequisite, pin it first in the given phase. Then hover and click the unpin button. The note title remains visible; the pinned heading is still present because of the seeded pinned note.

title: Pin note when creating it
rationale: Open the 'Take a note' editor, enter a unique title and content, click the pin control, and close the editor with Escape. The autosave should create the note and display it in the pinned section.

given.source: Unique scenario-derived title that does not collide with seeded notes; valid note title.
Unique scenario-derived content for the freshly created note; valid note content.

title: Initial suggested filters
rationale: The search bar is at the top of the home page. Clicking it reveals suggested filters. The seed contains a note titled 'Call dentist existing' with the 'Reminders' label and a note 'Movie list' without that label. Selecting the 'Reminders' filter should show only the note with that label. Navigation: open home, click search bar to focus it, then choose the suggested 'Reminders' filter. The filter result is observed by checking the presence of 'Call dentist existing' and absence of 'Movie list'.

title: Search by keyword
rationale: The search bar supports keyword input. The seed includes a note 'Study schedule' whose content contains the keyword 'st'. Typing 'st' and submitting the search should filter the notes to show that note. Highlighting of matching text is a visual styling that cannot be asserted via DOM text; therefore we assert the note appears and emit an unknown step for the highlight requirement.

then.detail: Highlighting of matching text cannot be observed via DOM text assertions.

title: Setting options list
rationale: Fresh browser session opens the application entry URL. The home page header exposes a settings icon with the accessible name 'Settings'. Clicking that button opens a dropdown whose menu includes a 'Settings' menu item; asserting that menu item is visible demonstrates the settings options list is displayed. No additional seed state is required for this check.

title: Detailed settings
rationale: After opening the home page, the settings icon is clicked to reveal the settings dropdown. Choosing the 'Settings' menu item navigates to the detailed settings screen. The detailed settings screen is expected to present configurable options together with save and cancel actions; therefore the Save and Cancel controls are asserted as visible. The route is inferred from the supplied navigation contract where 'Settings' in the settings dropdown leads to the detailed settings screen.

title: Toggle between list and grid views
rationale: The seeded home page displays notes such as 'Groceries'. Capturing the same note region before toggling, after switching to list view, and after switching back to grid view provides visual evidence of the layout change. Equality of the initial and final screenshots confirms the grid view was restored; inequality with the list-view screenshot confirms the switch to list view occurred.

title: Grid View by default
rationale: After opening the entry URL, the notes page is expected to start in grid view while the toolbar offers the list-view toggle. By capturing the default layout and then comparing it with the layout after switching to list view and back to grid view, the default state can be verified: equal to the final grid view and different from list view. The presence and operability of the list-view toggle also confirms the toolbar control exists.

title: Items and styling
rationale: Fresh browser opens '/' (home). The home page shows an open sidebar by default. Sidebar navigation items (Notes, Archived, Trash, Reminders) are accessible by their visible text. Consistent icons and styling are not directly observable through text/DOM, so that portion is marked unknown.

then.detail: Consistent icons and alignment styling cannot be verified via text/DOM observations.

title: Collapsible Sidebar
rationale: Fresh browser opens '/' with the sidebar expanded by default. The sidebar collapse control toggles between expanded and collapsed states. First click hides the 'Notes' text label (icon-only view); second click restores it. The target regex covers common accessible names for the collapse control.
